draft.title: Writing a historical explanation
card: A good historical explanation opens with a clear point. This is a one-sentence answer to the question, so the reader knows your argument straight away.
Next, back the point with evidence from sources. This might be a fact, a date or a short quote, and you say which source it came from.
Then explain how the evidence supports the point. Do not just drop in a quote. Say what it shows and why that matters for your argument.
Finish by linking back to the question. Show how your point helps answer what was asked.
draft.remember: Point, evidence, explain how the evidence fits, then link to the question.

a.q: A student writes a paragraph that has a clear point and a quote from a source. What is still missing?
opts: An explanation of how the quote supports the point
A second point that disagrees with the first
A longer quote taken from the same source
A summary of the whole unit of study
a.why: A quote alone does not prove anything. The student must say what it shows and how it backs up the point. A longer quote would still leave the reader to work out the meaning.
a.clue: Evidence needs the writer to say what it shows.

b.q: Asked why Viking raids caused fear in England, Sam writes: 'A monk wrote that the raiders were like wolves.' Which sentence would best finish this paragraph?
opts: This shows the monk saw the raiders as savage, so people feared them
The monk wrote many other things about life in the monastery
Vikings were sailors who travelled across the North Sea
Wolves were common animals in many parts of medieval Europe
b.why: The first option explains what the evidence shows and links it to the question about fear. The option about Viking sailors may be true, but it adds a new fact without explaining the evidence or answering the question.
b.clue: Which sentence ties the quote back to the question about fear?

b.q: Asked why Viking raids caused fear in England, Sam writes: 'The raids caused fear because they were violent. A monk wrote that the raiders were like wolves.' What should Sam write next?
opts: Calling them wolves shows the raiders seemed savage
Another monk also wrote about Viking ships on the coast
Vikings came from Scandinavia and sailed across the sea
Overall, that is why the Viking raids caused fear
b.why: Sam has a point and evidence, so the next step is to explain what the evidence shows. Calling the raiders wolves shows they seemed savage, which backs the point about violence. Jumping to 'that is why' skips the explanation and leaves the reader to work out what the quote means.
b.clue: Which step comes straight after the evidence?
